31 days at 110 degrees: Record heat tests Phoenix’s limits

"This story was originally published by Grist. Sign up for Grist's weekly newsletter here."

This story is part of Record High, a Grist series examining extreme heat and its impact on how — and where — we live.

The 1.6 million people who live in Phoenix, Arizona, just experienced the hottest month ever recorded in a city in the United States, according to the Arizona State Climate Office.

On Monday, the city’s high fell to 108 degrees Fahrenheit — a temperature that might only be considered a relief after the hellish run that Phoenix was on: 31 straight days that registered 110 degrees F or higher. Temperatures dipped slightly this week in the nation’s fifth-largest city, but they’re expected to climb again by the weekend.

“When you’re over 110 degrees, even if you’re born and raised here and you’re used to dealing with the heat, it’s still very hot and very dangerous for everyone,” said Erinanne Saffell, Arizona’s state climatologist.

The city’s average temperature in July was 102.7 degrees F, the highest ever measured in the U.S. outside of California’s Death Valley, a bone-dry desertscape that’s thought to be the hottest place in the world. Daytime highs in July averaged above 114 degrees F, and nighttime lows routinely stayed above 90 degrees F. In Arizona’s Maricopa County, the heat has been so severe and has lingered for so long that the medical examiner’s office recently added refrigeration units to keep up with deaths from the scorching weather.

Phoenix’s record-breaking temperatures are a microcosm of the world’s. Globally, July was the hottest month in 120,000 years. Scientists have warned that this summer’s extreme heat has been a sign of what’s to come as the planet warms. The outlook is grim. ... cnn.com/2023/07/17/weather/southwest-us-arizona-record-heat/index.html">told CNN in mid-July. Doctors have been placing patients in body bags filled with ice to cool down.

Nationwide, extreme heat could cost the U.S. $1 billion in healthcare expenses this summer alone by spurring 235,000 emergency room visits and 56,000 hospital admissions, according to one recent estimate. Most at risk are elderly people, outdoor workers, and those who don’t have access to indoor, air-conditioned spaces. In Phoenix, some residents are struggling to escape the stifling temperatures, as many of the city’s homeless shelters are full, the New York Times reported. So far this year, Maricopa County has reported 25 heat-related deaths and is investigating nearly 250 more.

**Minneapolis, also known as the City of Lakes** , has a population of 429,954. It’s located in Minnesota, in the Midwestern region of the United States in the Northern Hemisphere.

The unique climate of Minneapolis, Minnesota, can accommodate most desires at some point in the year. It’s not uncommon for snowbirds to call Minneapolis home; however, many residents love living there year-round. [44,000 Minnesotans also live part-time in other states](https://www.startribune.com/arizona-florida-naples-minnesota-snowbirds-retirees/600343995/) like Florida, Arizona, and Texas. ### Spring in Minneapolis The Minneapolis climate is typically most enjoyable from April to June. Spring weather means gradual warming, with temperatures ranging from 35 degrees Fahrenheit to 75 degrees Fahrenheit. Snow melts and gives way to blooming flowers and budding trees; you can delightfully watch Coneflowers, Geraniums, and Daylilies bloom throughout the city. Just remember to grab your umbrella, as rain showers are common during the spring months.
Despite heavy rainfall sometimes being an issue, residents still enjoy outdoor warm-weather activities like catching a Twins game at the Target Field or perusing the Minneapolis Sculpture Garden Art Fair. The average rainfall in March is 0.5 inches, and by June, it increases to 4.3 inches. The **average annual precipitation in Minneapolis is 32 inches.** ### Summer in Minneapolis The Summer months in Minneapolis are warm and pleasant, but humidity is present. Temperatures are typically in the 70s, but the **Minneapolis summer high temperatures** are in the mid-80s **.** The average summer humidity level in Minneapolis is 64.8%. Due to the [urban heat island effect](https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/what-is-an-urban-heat-island/) , downtown Minneapolis can experience extreme heat levels. In fact, some areas that are located in more [urbanized areas of Minneapolis can see heat increases of more than 9 degrees higher](https://environment.umn.

...

### Fall in Minneapolis Vibrant foliage and colder temps mean Minneapolis fall is in full swing! Grab your pumpkin spice latte—you’ve got fall festivals to explore and autumn weather to enjoy! **Minneapolis Hard Cider & Doughnut Fest takes place in September,** and “Horn-ucopia” Fall Funk Fest is in October, but there are many more events and things to check out during Minneapolis autumn. September, October, and November are the last few comfortable months before the region's intense winter takes over. By November, the daily high is only 34 degrees Fahrenheit, and temperatures can reach the low 20s. **Autumn in Minneapolis** is beautiful but short-lived; come November, snowfall is already wreaking havoc. ### Winter in Minneapolis Once December rolls around, Minneapolitans are bundled up and hunkering down for some cold temps and snow days ahead. **Minneapolis's winter weather** is just what you’d expect from a Minnesota city: cold and snowy. **On average, Minneapolis gets 37.
1 inches of snow in the winter months.** The average daily high from November to early March is 36 degrees Fahrenheit. Minneapolis’s coldest month is January, with an average daily temperature of 10 degrees. Minneapolis's winter precipitation is pretty much constant; the chance of a wet day is around 11% throughout the winter. Although cold, there are still plenty of **Minneapolis winter activities** to partake in! You can explore the Northeast Winter Market at Quincy Hall or check out the Nordic Village at Riva Terrace. One of the top things to do in Minneapolis in the winter is the St. Paul Winter Carnival! While temperatures can dip below freezing, **Minneapolis is not the coldest US state, Alaska is!** Although residents tend to peg March as Minnepaolis snowiest month, [data shows it’s actually December](https://mix108.com/minnesota-snowiest-months-of-the-year/) , with an average snowfall of around 11.4 inches—talk about a white Christmas!
## Minneapolis Monthly Weather | Minneapolis Monthly Average Temperature Here is a look at the **Minneapolis weather by month** and what to expect after relocating to Minneapolis. Humid conditions and hot temperatures are apparent in the summer, and cold winters are unavoidable. Heavy rainfalls are typical in the springtime. Each season boasts its own distinct characteristics that can be appealing to anyone. ### January January's average temperature is 16.2 degrees Fahrenheit, but it can range anywhere from 28 degrees to 8.9 degrees. Thus, January is typically the coldest month in Minneapolis. Cold weather means winter activities! The top things to do in Minneapolis in winter include ice skating at The Depot Ice Rink or Centennial Lakes Park; you can participate in the Saint Paul Winter Carnival, which includes ice sculptures, parades, and winter activities. ### February February’s average temperature is 21.8 degrees Fahrenheit, ranging from the high 20s to around 15 degrees.
While it’s slightly warmer than January, February in Minneapolis is still very cold, with plenty of snow. Love Month brings Valentine's Day events galore, alongside the notable Loppet Ski Festival, with cross-country ski races, ice biking, and other winter sports activities. ### March March temperatures are finally rising, and the spring season is just around the corner. The average daily temperature in March is 33.8 degrees Fahrenheit, and it can get as warm as 41.4 degrees. The average low is 26 degrees. Minneapolis has a notable Irish population, with about [600,000 residents of Irish descent](https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/good-question-how-irish-are-minnesotans/) , meaning St. Patty’s Day is a serious holiday here. The city has a large parade in downtown Minneapolis. You can also visit the Como Park Zoo and Conservatory for the seasonal flower show. ### April In Minneapolis, April is the month of warmer temperatures and rain showers.

...

If you're a runner, take advantage of the beautiful weather by participating in the Twin Cities Marathon. ### October October's average temperature is 50.8 degrees Fahrenheit, with an average high of 59 degrees and an average low of 42.6 degrees. October is a beautiful month for fall foliage and outdoor activities! One of the top things to do in Minneapolis in the fall is enjoy the autumn colors at parks like Minnehaha Falls and along the Mississippi River. The Twin Cities Film Fest is another popular event residents adore. ### November In November, the average temperature in Minneapolis is 35 degrees Fahrenheit. The temperature range includes an average high of 41.8 degrees and an average low of 28.1 degrees. **With colder temperatures and the first snowfalls, November marks the transition to winter** . November in the Twin Cities is considered dry, with minimal precipitation. You can get your Christmas shopping done at the various holiday markets and fairs throughout the city.

 ## Extreme Weather in Minneapolis Minneapolis has a variety of extreme weather conditions. * Very cold winters: Minneapolis is known for its harsh winters with extremely low temperatures, heavy snowfall, freezing rain, and frequent blizzards. Temperatures can drop below -30°F, and the city often faces strong winds and ice storms. Minneapolis can be colder than most major metropolitan areas in the United States.
* Heat waves: While summers are generally warm, Minneapolis can experience heat waves with temperatures soaring above 90°F and occasionally reaching over 100°F.
* Thunderstorms: Spring and summer bring frequent thunderstorms, which can sometimes be severe. These storms can produce heavy rain, hail, and strong winds.
